summary: Candidate 5 rejects every exact member of the independently derived 57-path and 30-identifier forbidden inventory as both JSON keys and string values, flat and nested, through both blind-mode input locations before write; all 1,392 exact real-CLI cases preserved absent or sentinel outputs. All 26 justified shared source-only identifiers remained usable in 208 cases, and 208 exact forbidden descendants under those shared keys were rejected. One concrete bypass remains: object keys are compared to forbidden identifiers only by whole-key equality. A colon-delimited forbidden identifier is therefore a lexical token but not the whole key. All 30 forbidden identifiers were admitted in that form through both packet and completeness inputs with absent and sentinel outputs (120/120 real-CLI admissions). A dedicated rootCauseId reproduction confirmed the exact key bytes were serialized into both emitted blind prompts, creating absent outputs and overwriting sentinel bytes.

findings.title: Delimiter-wrapped post-reveal identifier keys bypass blind prewrite filtering
findings.contract: Before either blind canonical prompt input is emitted, every forbidden post-reveal identifier occurring as a lexical identifier token must be rejected in JSON values and object member names. Explicitly shared source-only identifiers may remain usable, but cannot suppress recursive rejection of a forbidden descendant.
findings.claim: source_only_payload_failures applies lexical-token matching to string values but tests object member names only for exact set membership. A nested key such as leak:rootCauseId:field contains rootCauseId as a colon-delimited lexical token under the same boundary used for values, yet returns no source-only failure. The real blind CLI then serializes that key into the prompt.

evidence.detail: The dict branch at lines 160-171 rejects an identifier only when key in forbidden_identifiers. The string branch at lines 183-190 rejects the same inventory member with explicit left and right lexical boundaries. Therefore leak:rootCauseId:field is rejected as a value but admitted as a key.

main computes canonical_prompt_bytes at line 332 before mkdir/write at lines 338-339. This correctly preserves outputs for detected payloads, but admitted keys reach output.write_bytes and are serialized.

The candidate-5 inventory control covers every identifier as a value and an exact whole key, but does not exercise a lexically delimited identifier within a member name or either real CLI output state.

The real-CLI adversarial-identifier-key-wrapper category contains 120/120 exit-0 admissions: all 30 forbidden identifiers, both blind input locations, and both absent/sentinel initial states. All rendered keys use colon boundaries; programmatic classification found 120 lexical-token cases and zero arbitrary-substring-only cases.

A separate real-CLI reproduction used nested key leak:rootCauseId:field under the allowed shared key path. All four runs (packet/completeness x absent/sentinel) exited 0, found the exact JSON key in emitted bytes, created absent outputs, and overwrote sentinel outputs. rootCauseId matched lexical span [5,16] in the key.

Preserved emitted packet-mode prompt. Line 33 contains {"outer": [{"path": {"leak:rootCauseId:field": "post-reveal-value"}}]}. The packet-sentinel reproduction emitted byte-identical prompt SHA-256 8c3dc9f8cbe044f764471012510227b1722d260c99aa4b32b4e90d059b0ae5f9.

Preserved emitted completeness-mode prompt. Line 38 contains the same exact key. The completeness-sentinel reproduction emitted byte-identical prompt SHA-256 e4ba69d1524c5df4497543587bd520c99d66c9155828264ca62a6582d0dcf374.

reproduction.commandTemplate: python3 scripts/build_correctness_audit_prompt.py --mode blind --packet <canonical packet> --completeness <canonical review> --output <canonical prompts output>
reproduction.observed: For packet and completeness placement, both an absent output and a pre-existing binary sentinel produced CLI exit 0. The absent output was created; the sentinel SHA-256 c3eab0df90d9c81ced790c3595bece504dd55f1761d9e16dd5fac3caab9d1998 was replaced; the exact forbidden-key bytes were present in each emitted prompt.
reproduction.expected: All four invocations must fail before creating or modifying output because rootCauseId is a forbidden post-reveal identifier serialized as a delimited lexical token in a member name.

findings.impact: A source packet or accepted completeness-review JSON can expose any closed post-reveal comparison/adjudication identifier to the isolated blind reviewer by surrounding it with punctuation in a JSON member name. Because the prompt builder does not schema-validate these payloads before serialization, later schema rejection cannot restore blindness once the prompt bytes have been written or sent.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same escaped lexical-token matcher used for string values to every object member name, while retaining exact shared-identifier exemptions only for the shared token itself. Add inventory-driven real-CLI controls for every forbidden identifier in delimiter-wrapped keys, in packet and completeness inputs, nested under each class of allowed shared key, with absent-parent, absent-file, and byte-identical sentinel assertions.

outputBytePreservationEvidence.sourceWriteOrdering: canonical_output_path is checked first; canonical_prompt_bytes and all source-only validation run at line 332; only then do lines 338-339 create the parent and write bytes. Dynamic rejected cases confirm this order. The finding reaches the write only because key matching returns no failure.
